_comment: USER-FOUND, 2026-09-03 (play viewer, rejection artifact s1_gi0_t2): 'Wild growth mana is not
being considered'. A land Aura's additional mana is credited by the PAYMENT solver and by the
real tap, but BOTH colour gates walked each source's own EffectiveProduces and never looked at
the Auras attached to it -- ComputeAvailableColors (TurnSolver.cpp, colour PRESENCE) and
BuildColorFeasibility (ManaPayment.cpp, colour EXACT). So a cast whose coloured pip was payable
only off an aura was pruned before the payer ever saw it.
NOT a viewer bug. Both gates are built once per enumeration at the SEARCH's two plan
enumerators, so the search dropped the same lines in every game of every seed; the viewer's
line validator merely named the reason out loud. In BuildColorFeasibility the COUNT was already
right (PermanentManaYield adds LandAuraBonus) -- the units were just being credited under the
HOST's colours, so a Wild Growth on an Adarkar Wastes read as 'two mana of W/U/C'.
The fixture: Adarkar Wastes makes W/U/C and Mariposa Military Base makes {C} -- NO red on the
board. Fertile Ground on the Wastes adds one mana of ANY colour, which is the only thing that
can pay the {R} in Shivan Gorge's '{2}{R}, {T}: deals 1 damage to each opponent'. Three mana
available, one of them red-capable, so the Gorge fires exactly once.
Verified DISCRIMINATING: delete the Fertile Ground entry and the board still makes three mana
but none of it red -- the Gorge cannot be activated and the opponent stays on 20 (against 18
with it). The aura is the only difference and the COLOUR it supplies is the only thing under
test. active_life 18 is the Adarkar Wastes pain on each coloured tap, which is the second
witness that the enchanted land is the one being tapped.
FOUR sites were blind, and only the fourth made the fixture move: the two colour gates above,
the payment DFS (TapForCostBacktrackWorker -- `amt` was ManaProducedPerTap, so an enchanted
land tapped for exactly what it prints), and TapFlowInfeasible, the flow oracle, which can
declare a cost infeasible and short-circuit the payment before the DFS ever runs. Only
AddSourceToPool (the greedy pool path) was ever correct, which is why the deck still ramped and
the bug stayed hidden.
Deliberately avoids hybrid costs: Vexing Shusher ({R/G}{R/G}) was the first choice here and it
turned out to be uncastable off green, which is a SEPARATE open bug -- see the ledger.
